supporting_observations.claim: ana.ruiz ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-PIN-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ana.ruiz\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon then recorded creation of that archive.
Minutes later, Edge was launched to dropzone-transfer.net, a file-transfer destination not listed among the organization’s approved services.

The recorded proxy request to dropzone-transfer.net was rejected with status 407 (authentication required); the accompanying connection record shows a small exchange with the internal proxy, not evidence of a completed large external upload.
The archive-then-transfer-site sequence is suspicious and consistent with attempted exfiltration, but the available records do not establish that any client files were successfully uploaded.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records do not show the archive’s contents, size, or whether it contained client data.
The proxy record shows the destination request was rejected, but the evidence does not establish whether a later attempt succeeded through another path or at another time.
The provided records do not include evidence confirming the alert’s reported large outbound transfer.
claims_not_established: That c.zip contained client data or was successfully transferred off the workstation.
That the 13:46 activity resulted in a completed large outbound transfer.
Whether ana.ruiz had authorization for the archive creation or any attempted transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy records for the destination around and after 13:46 UTC, including any authenticated retry, upload method, request size, and final status.
Endpoint evidence for c.zip, including file size, hash, contents or metadata, and subsequent access or deletion.
Network-flow or egress records that can confirm or rule out a large transfer from WS-ARUIZ-01 during the alert window.
Relevant user or business context establishing whether the archive creation or transfer was authorized.
